name: Industrial DP/correlation geosteering patents: US 11180981 B2 (Chevron, automated post-geosteering by dynamic programming) and US 11480045 B2 (assigned to RNA Capital Inc., not Chevron: methods for assisted and automated horizontal-well geosteering)
authors_org: US11180981: Julian A. Thorne, Chevron U.S.A. Inc. US11480045: Ivan Denisenko, Oleg Kushmantsev, Igor Uvarov, Igor Kuvaev; assignee RNA Capital Inc. The inventor list suggests a ROGII-affiliated origin (Igor Uvarov is also the name of ROGII's founder) [uncertain].
venue_link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US11180981 (family: US20200165911A1, WO2020109890A1, EP3887637B1, CN113227529B, AU2019387627B2, AR117152A1) ; https://patents.google.com/patent/US11480045
code_availability: No code. US11180981 states its recurrence at pseudocode level, so it is easy to reimplement; US11480045 describes a multi-algorithm workflow without implementable detail for its neural-network component.
evidence_level: Granted patents (legal disclosure, not peer-reviewed); illustrative synthetic and field figures only, no quantitative benchmark.
extreme_summary: US11180981 post-geosteers a lateral with a DP over (lateral sample, pilot-well index): std-normalized |GR| mismatch cost, a smoothness penalty on index jumps and a penalty pulling toward the survey-based path, then a min-cost backtrack; the mapping may go up and down section. US11480045 splits the lateral into overlapping segments, scores many dip hypotheses per segment with a weighted similarity K-value (Pearson, RMS deviation, dip-change penalties), detects re-crossings by self-correlation, and reports per-segment confidence plus a 'geosteering spectrum' of alternatives.
task_definition: Estimate the stratigraphic position (TVT / typewell index) of each lateral sample from the lateral LWD log and one or more typewell (pilot) logs; US11180981 post-drill (retro-steering), US11480045 in real time as MWD/LWD data arrive.
inputs: US11180981: pilot (typewell) log, lateral log, initial well path from gyro/survey. US11480045: one or more typewell logs, lateral MWD/LWD logs, trajectory, regional dip ranges, formation-thickness constraints.
target_parameterisation: US11180981: typewell sample index n(ns) per lateral sample ns (equivalent to TVT). US11480045: piecewise-linear formation dip per segment (explicit dip state), from which TVT follows.
output_representation: US11180981: single min-cost path. US11480045: best-scoring interpretation, per-segment confidence factors, and a 2D similarity spectrum over (dip, MD) showing alternative interpretations.
architecture: US11180981: cost[n][ns] = |pilot[n]/sd_pilot - lateral[ns]/sd_lateral|; mincost[n][ns] = min over m of (mincost[m][ns-1] + smoothbias*|m-n|) + cost[n][ns] + pathbias*|pathw[ns]-n|; backtrack from the minimum at the last lateral sample. US11480045: overlapping 'big segments'; per segment several similarity algorithms (MSE, Pearson, cumulative absolute difference, and a neural network trained on original plus synthetically distorted logs, scoring by Euclidean distance in an n-dimensional embedding); K-value combines correlation T, RMS deviation SQ and dip differences with tunable exponents pow1-pow5; the algorithm/dip with the highest K wins; local-extremum search tests several extrema penalized against the previous segment's dip; self-correlation and repeated-section methods detect re-entry into the same formation; when new data arrive the method steps back a fixed depth and reprocesses.
core_mechanism: Non-monotone alignment: the state is the typewell level at each lateral sample, and transitions penalize level change instead of forbidding backward moves, so the path can go up and down section. An extra prior ties the solution to the survey trajectory (pathbias), acting as a drift regularizer. US11480045 adds explicit dip-continuity scoring and multi-hypothesis display with confidence.
training_objective: US11180981: none (smoothbias/pathbias set by the operator or automatically). US11480045: a similarity network trained on original logs plus synthetically distorted copies (metric-learning style); the K-value is hand-weighted.
decoding: US11180981: Viterbi-style min-cost backtrack (mode). US11480045: argmax K-value per segment with sequential dip continuity (greedy/local), plus alternative extrema for review.
metric_consistent_decode: Mode-seeking in both. For our pooled RMSE the Bayes-optimal counterpart is the expectation over the same lattice (as in the 2nd-place DP); the 2nd-place author found Viterbi consistently worse than the expectation.
evidence_scope: US11180981: whole lateral jointly against one pilot well. US11480045: overlapping segments, multiple typewells.
prefix_conditioning: US11180981: start point and pathbias toward the initial path; no learned use of known heel labels. US11480045: previous segments' dips constrain the next segment (sequential).
propose_vs_select: US11180981: single path. US11480045: candidate generation (several algorithms and extrema) plus selection by K-value; the spectrum is effectively a hypothesis set.
physical_constraints: Smooth stratigraphic position (index jumps penalized); adherence to survey trajectory; in US11480045 also regional dip range, bounded dip change between adjacent segments, formation-thickness bounds.
dataset: US11180981: one synthetic example and three field GR cases. US11480045: unspecified field wells.
synthetic_to_real: US11180981: std normalization of each log. US11480045: scale normalization of typewell to lateral; similarity NN trained on synthetic distortions of real logs (augmentation-style synthetic data).
metric_and_performance: No quantitative metrics. US11180981 shows the corrected path closely matching the true path in a synthetic case and plausible modelled-vs-observed GR on field cases.
comparability: Not comparable (no numbers). Conceptually US11180981 is a hand-crafted analogue of the 2nd-place AnchorCNN + DP, with fixed costs where the 2nd place learns move distributions.
inference_budget: US11180981 naive O(N_lateral * N_pilot^2), or O(N_lateral * N_pilot * W) with a bounded jump window: well under a second per well on CPU for a 345 x 400 grid. US11480045 heavier but still CPU-cheap.
repeated_layers: US11180981: only smoothness and pathbias break ties between self-similar levels; no multi-hypothesis output. US11480045: explicitly handles re-crossing via self-correlation and repeated-section detection, tests multiple local extrema, and exposes ambiguity through the spectrum and low-confidence flags for geologist review.
drift: US11180981's pathbias pulls the solution toward the survey trajectory, an explicit prior against slow drift. US11480045 bounds dip change between segments and to a regional range, i.e. an explicit dip state.
uncertainty_and_calibration: US11180981: none. US11480045: per-segment confidence factor and similarity spectrum (uncalibrated).
where_to_use: (1) Confirms the 2nd-place design (DP over typewell level per lateral column with a move penalty); keep the sum-product expectation, not the patent's min-cost path. (2) The pathbias idea maps to a trajectory/structural prior (cf. item A18, TVT + Z identity), best introduced as an input channel rather than a hard decode term. (3) US11480045's dip-state scoring maps to a second-order (level, previous move) state in the AnchorCNN DP, and its confidence output to a per-well flag.
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) via pathbias / dip-continuity priors; band confusion (~51%) only indirectly (multi-hypothesis exposure, confidence).
gap_vs_our_implementation: Already have: DP over (MD column, TVT level) with learned move distributions (2nd-place AnchorCNN) and expectation decode, which is stronger than the patent's min-cost path. Gaps: (a) the 2nd-place DP is first-order in level, P(dTVT | anchor at level, column), with no explicit dip/rate state; US11480045 scores dip continuity, and a (level, dip) state is the principled version. (b) No path-level prior toward a structurally/trajectory-consistent path (pathbias analogue); the ConvNeXt path has none at all. (c) No per-well or per-segment confidence output used for anything. (d) US11480045 allows multiple typewells per lateral; our inputs use a single typewell (plus the 2nd-place self-prefix reference).
proposed_experiment: A04-1 (dip-state DP, no retraining): in the kaggle2ndplace inference DP (eq. 5 of 2nd.txt), expand the state from level s to (s, d), d = previous move bin (21 classes); transition P(s', d' | s, d) = P_anchor(d' | s, k) * g(d' - d), g a fixed Gaussian on move change fitted on TRAINING wells (analogous to the 0.78 ft per-column std measured in posterior_fb_decode.py), renormalized. Keep expectation decode. Compare with the current first-order DP on the 155 holdout wells using the same AnchorCNN checkpoints; state size 128 x 21 per column is cheap. Also sweep g's width including infinity (which recovers the baseline) on training wells only. A04-2 (pathbias as evidence, not decode): since the hard-continuity decode failed on ConvNeXt posteriors, add a channel with a Gaussian ridge at the prefix-extrapolated TVT (TVT_last + prefix rate * dMD, sigma growing with distance from the heel) to the ConvNeXt input; 60 ep vs identical control, >0.39 ft required. A04-3 (baseline, ~1 day): reimplement US11180981 verbatim with smoothbias/pathbias tuned on training wells; report holdout RMSE and error correlation with ConvNeXt/FastViT to size the gap between hand-crafted DP and learned models.
implementation_effort: A04-1 medium (modify the 2nd-place DP inference, check normalization; no training). A04-2 medium (new channel + retrain). A04-3 low (~100 lines numba).
gpu_cost: A04-1: inference only, trivial even with a 21x larger state (< 1 s per well). A04-2: one 60-epoch ConvNeXt retrain (hours on RTX 5060 8 GB). A04-3: CPU only.
distillation_compatibility: A04-1 applies after AnchorCNN outputs, independent of the FastViT student (its DP marginals could also serve as soft KD targets). A04-2's channel is KD-compatible. A04-3 not applicable.
error_correlation_with_ours: Hand-crafted DP (A04-3): moderately low correlation expected but much higher error [uncertain]. Dip-state DP (A04-1): high correlation with the current AnchorCNN DP (same emissions); it should mainly change drift-type errors.
risk: (1) Patents provide no benchmark; the ideas are standard DP engineering. (2) Our continuity forward-backward decode already failed on ConvNeXt posteriors because smoothing locks onto wrong bands; a dip-state DP may likewise sharpen onto wrong modes and lose the averaging benefit of the expectation. (3) AnchorCNN move distributions already see local context that encodes dip, so explicit dip continuity may add less than the 0.39 ft noise floor. (4) A pathbias-style prior only helps when structural dip is small; a strong trajectory prior would bias wells with real dip changes. (5) US11180981 is in force until about 2040: fine for research, relevant for commercial deployment.
notes: Correction to the outline: US11480045 is assigned to RNA Capital Inc., not Chevron; it likely reflects the StarSteer-style workflow of the competition host [uncertain]. US11180981 explicitly cites Hladil et al. 2010 (DTW log correlation) and argues that because laterals go up and down, a more complex mapping than monotone DTW is needed, which is the same rationale as the 2nd-place DP. Prior art it cites: US20050171698A1 (real-time earth-model geosteering), WO2014160741A1 (automatic geosteering with evolutionary algorithms). Citing documents include US11971513B2 and US20250369288A1 (AI-assisted stratigraphic modeling with GR).
